summary: A 1931 L-4 pole lookout on St. Joe National Forest was replaced in 1964 by an R-6 flattop tower, now on emergency status and rented through the Forest Service's cabin program.

facts.design: 15'x15' R-6 flattop cab with catwalk on a treated-timber tower
facts.status_note: Described as on 'emergency status' rather than actively staffed, per firelookout.com

access.note: Reached via a rugged single-lane road with pullouts, not recommended for low-clearance vehicles.

visit.trail_note: Road can be slick when wet; not recommended for low-clearance vehicles.

events.note: First lookout: gabled L-4 cab on a 20-ft pole tower, on the St. Joe National Forest
Replaced by current R-6 15'x15' flattop cab with catwalk on a timber tower

evidence.supports: 1931 original L-4 on pole tower; 1964 replacement with R-6 flattop
evidence.quote: The first lookout on Surveyor's Ridge on the St. Joe National Forest was a gabled L-4 on a 20' pole tower built in 1931. In 1964 it was replaced by the current R-6 15' x 15' flattop with catwalk on a 20' timber tower.

evidence.supports: overlooks Mallard-Larkins Pioneer Area, added to cabin rental program
evidence.quote: In active service until recent years the lookout -- which overlooks the Mallard-Larkins Pioneer Area -- has been added to the cabin rental program.

evidence.supports: 1931 built with L-4 cab on 20-ft pole tower; 1964 replacement with R-6 flat cab on 20-ft timber tower
evidence.quote: First used in 1931 with a 20' pole tower and L-4 cab, the present 20' treated timber tower with R-6 flat cab was built in 1964.

evidence.supports: emergency status, now on rental program, listed on NHLR
evidence.quote: On emergency status for several years, the tower is presently available on the Recreation Rental program, and is listed on the National Historic Lookout Register.

evidence.supports: two additional patrol lookout sites nearby
evidence.quote: There were also patrol lookout sites 1 1/4 miles to the northeast and 2 1/2 miles to the east atop Surveyors Peak.

evidence.supports: sits atop a 30-ft tower per recreation.gov (conflicts with 20-ft given by NHLR/firelookout.com)
evidence.quote: Located near the Mallard-Larkins Pioneer Area Attractions, Surveyors Lookout is perched atop a 30 foot tower, providing phenomenal views of Snow Peak and the surrounding mountains.
Access to the lookout is via a rugged single-lane road with pullouts, and is not recommended for low clearance vehicles. Road may be slick when wet.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and firelookout.com both describe a 20-ft timber tower built in 1964, while recreation.gov states the lookout sits atop a 30-ft tower. The story notes this disagreement rather than picking one figure; the brief's height_m (6.1m, i.e. ~20ft) matches the NHLR/firelookout.com figure and was left unchanged.

sources.title: Surveyors Lookout, Idaho Panhandle National Forests

notes_for_editor: No source gives a specific year staffing ended; firelookout.com's 'emergency status for several years' phrasing was used as-is. Sources conflict on tower height (20ft vs 30ft) -- flagged in resolved_conflicts and in the story rather than resolved. Removed an unsupported 'network'/'Upper St. Joe country' characterization and an unsupported 1930s-1960s service-span claim from the story; neither was backed by a source quote.
